name: Settela Steinbach
milestone_by_age_26: Died at age 9 in Auschwitz in 1944; no career milestone possible. Fame is entirely posthumous from a film image taken at Westerbork.
early_history_summary: Settela Steinbach was a Dutch Sinti girl born in 1934 who was deported to Westerbork and then Auschwitz, where she was gassed at age 9 in 1944. She became known posthumously as 'the girl with the headscarf' from film footage shot at Westerbork, identified only in the 1990s.
family_context_summary: Born into a traditional Sinti family in Buchten, Netherlands; father was a trader and violinist, mother ran the household while traveling from village to village.
evidence_summary: Settela Steinbach was a child victim of the Holocaust, murdered at age 9. She had no career or agency; her fame derives entirely from being filmed at Westerbork transit camp by Rudolf Breslauer. She was identified as a Sinti girl only in the 1990s by journalist Aad Wagenaar. No milestone by age 26 is possible.

name: Carlo Rovelli
milestone_by_age_26: Received Laurea in Physics from University of Bologna in 1981 at age 25, but this is a standard degree, not a material milestone. PhD started in 1983 at age 27; first post-doc in 1987 at age 31. No independently verifiable material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Rovelli was born in Verona, Italy, and attended Liceo Classico Scipione Maffei. He participated in student political movements in the 1970s and took seven years to complete his undergraduate degree at the University of Bologna, graduating with honors in 1981. He began his PhD at the University of Padua in 1983.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond being born in Verona, Italy.
evidence_summary: Rovelli's early career was delayed by political activism and extended undergraduate studies. He received his Laurea in Physics from Bologna in 1981 at age 25, but his significant research contributions (loop quantum gravity, relational quantum mechanics) came in the late 1980s and 1990s. His first post-doctoral position was at Yale in 1987 (age 31). No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Erhard Loretan
milestone_by_age_26: By age 25 (1984), had climbed five 8,000-meter peaks including a first ascent of Annapurna's east ridge and the first winter ascent of Dhaulagiri, establishing himself as one of the world's leading high-altitude alpinists.
early_history_summary: Born in Bulle, Switzerland, Loretan climbed his first mountain at age 11 and made his first north face ascent at 14. He trained as a cabinet maker in 1979 and became a certified mountain guide in 1981. He began climbing 8,000-meter peaks in 1982 with Nanga Parbat and in 1983 climbed three such peaks (Gasherbrum II, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak) in just 17 days.
primary_leverage_engine: Early alpine specialization and physical talent
family_context_summary: Born in Bulle in the canton of Fribourg, Switzerland; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond geographic origin at the foot of the Alps.
primary_early_advantage_tags: alpine geography, early climbing start, mountain guide pipeline, climbing partners
evidence_summary: Loretan was born in Bulle, Switzerland, at the foot of the Alps, and began climbing at age 11. By his mid-teens he was doing serious alpine routes, and he became a mountain guide at 22. His geographic immersion in the Swiss Alps provided direct access to the world's premier mountaineering training ground. By age 25, he had climbed five 8,000-meter peaks including a first ascent of Annapurna, applying fast-and-light alpine style to the Himalayas. No family financial or domain advantage is documented; his achievement appears driven by early geographic immersion and self-driven repetition.
starting_point: Born in Bulle, canton of Fribourg, Switzerland; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond geographic origin at the foot of the Alps.
current_position: Died in 2011 at age 52 in a mountaineering accident on the Grünhorn, Bernese Oberland; final role: mountain guide and climber, third person to climb all 14 eight-thousanders.

trajectory.event: Climbed Dent de Broc, his first mountain.
Became a certified mountain guide after training as a cabinet maker.
Climbed Nanga Parbat, his first 8,000-meter peak.
Completed first ascent of Annapurna's east ridge with Norbert Joos and first winter ascent of Dhaulagiri.
Climbed Mount Everest in 40 hours without supplementary oxygen with Jean Troillet.
Climbed Kangchenjunga, completing all 14 eight-thousanders, the third person to do so.
Died in a climbing accident on the Grünhorn while guiding clients.

name: David Coverdale
milestone_by_age_26: Became lead singer of Deep Purple in 1973 at age 22 and recorded the album Burn (February 1974), which reached the top 10 in multiple countries, making him the frontman of one of the world's biggest rock bands before age 26.
early_history_summary: Coverdale was born in Saltburn-by-the-Sea, Yorkshire, and began performing with local bands at age 15, starting with Vintage 67 in 1966. He played with The Government (1968-1972) and Fabulosa Brothers (1972-1973) while attending art college and working as a salesman. In 1973, after seeing a Melody Maker ad, he auditioned for Deep Purple and was selected as Ian Gillan's replacement.
primary_leverage_engine: Years of local band performance and vocal ability
family_context_summary: Born in Saltburn-by-the-Sea, Yorkshire; father was out of work and family faced economic difficulties. Grew up above a club run by his parents, which exposed him to music via the jukebox. Maternal side were singers, paternal side were artists.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother's side of the family were singers; paternal side were painters and sketchers. Coverdale was initiated into music at his maternal grandmother's place and started learning guitar and piano at an early age.
primary_early_advantage_tags: local band reps, family music exposure, mentor Jon Lord, economic hardship, hard rock wave
evidence_summary: Coverdale grew up in modest circumstances in Yorkshire with economic difficulties at home, but was exposed to music through his family and the club his parents ran. He spent seven years performing with local bands before auditioning for Deep Purple in 1973. Jon Lord of Deep Purple became an important mentor. The 1970s hard rock wave and Deep Purple's status as one of the world's biggest bands provided the platform for his early fame. His family's musical background provided early exposure but no financial platform.
starting_point: Born in Saltburn-by-the-Sea, Yorkshire, England; father was out of work and family faced economic difficulties; grew up above a club run by his parents with exposure to music via the jukebox.
current_position: Retired from music in 2025; formerly lead singer of Whitesnake and Deep Purple; resides in Lake Tahoe, Nevada; inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2016.

trajectory.event: Began performing with local band Vintage 67 in Yorkshire.
Joined Deep Purple as lead singer, replacing Ian Gillan.
Released Burn, his first album with Deep Purple, which became a major commercial success.
Founded Whitesnake, the band that would define his career.
Whitesnake's self-titled album went multi-platinum with hit singles 'Here I Go Again' and 'Is This Love'.
Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Deep Purple.
Retired from active performing after Whitesnake's farewell tour.

name: Tony Esposito
milestone_by_age_26: Won the NCAA Championship with Michigan Tech in 1965 (age 22) as a three-time All-American, then made his NHL debut with Montreal Canadiens in 1968-69 and was part of the Stanley Cup championship team at age 26.
early_history_summary: Esposito grew up in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, playing hockey from childhood with his older brother Phil, a future NHL star. He played college hockey at Michigan Tech, where he was a three-time first-team All-American and helped win the 1964-65 NCAA Championship. He turned professional in 1967 and reached the NHL with Montreal in 1968-69.
primary_leverage_engine: Hockey family immersion and collegiate pipeline
family_context_summary: Born in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario; father Pat worked at the Algoma steel plant. Older brother Phil Esposito became an NHL Hall of Famer. Working-class family with strong hockey culture.
parent_family_domain_summary: Hockey was part of the family fabric; both Tony and older brother Phil played from an early age. Phil became one of the NHL's greatest players, providing a high-trust peer and domain model in the household.
primary_early_advantage_tags: NCAA championship, brother Phil Esposito, Michigan Tech, Glenn Hall mentorship, hockey family
evidence_summary: Esposito grew up in a working-class family in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, where hockey was embedded in the family culture. His older brother Phil became an NHL star, providing both a peer model and access to professional hockey networks. Tony's three-time All-American career at Michigan Tech and the 1965 NCAA Championship provided an elite collegiate pipeline. He learned from Glenn Hall through his brother's connections. By age 26, he had won an NCAA title, made his NHL debut, and been part of a Stanley Cup championship team with Montreal.
starting_point: Born in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, Canada; father worked at the Algoma steel plant; older brother Phil Esposito became an NHL Hall of Famer; working-class hockey family.
current_position: Died in 2021 at age 78 in Chicago, Illinois; final role: retired NHL goaltender, Hockey Hall of Famer, and Chicago Blackhawks ambassador; named one of the 100 Greatest NHL Players in 2017.

trajectory.event: Won NCAA Championship with Michigan Tech and was named first-team NCAA All-Tournament.
Made NHL debut with Montreal Canadiens, playing 13 games in relief during the 1968-69 season.
Was part of the Montreal Canadiens Stanley Cup championship team.
Won Calder Trophy as NHL rookie of the year with Chicago Blackhawks, setting a modern record of 15 shutouts in a season.
Represented Canada in the Summit Series against the Soviet Union, splitting goaltending duties with Ken Dryden.
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame; jersey number 35 retired by Chicago Blackhawks.
Died in Chicago, Illinois.

name: Yuan Longping
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from Southwest Agricultural College in 1953 at age 23 and was assigned to teach at a small agricultural school in Hunan. No material research milestone by age 26; his hybrid rice breakthroughs came in the 1960s-1970s.
early_history_summary: Yuan was born in Beijing in 1930 to parents who were both teachers. He entered Southwest Agricultural College in 1949 to study agriculture and crop genetics, graduating in 1953. He was assigned to teach agronomy at Anjiang Agricultural School in Hunan province, where he remained until 1971. He began researching rice male sterility in 1964, leading to his hybrid rice breakthroughs in the 1970s.
family_context_summary: Born in Beijing to parents who were both teachers; family moved frequently during the Second Sino-Japanese War and Chinese Civil War, attending school in Hunan, Chongqing, Hankou, and Nanjing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having direct agricultural domain expertise; parents were teachers with no family background in farming.
evidence_summary: Yuan graduated from Southwest Agricultural College in 1953 and was assigned to teach at a remote agricultural school in Hunan. His research on hybrid rice began in 1964 (age 34), with the first successful hybrid varieties developed in 1973 (age 43). The Great Leap Forward famine (1958-60) deeply motivated his work, but no material research milestone occurred by age 26. His fame as the 'Father of Hybrid Rice' came decades later.

name: John E. Walker
milestone_by_age_26: Received BA in Chemistry from Oxford in 1964 (age 23) and began doctoral research in 1965, but no material research milestone by age 26. D.Phil awarded in 1969 (age 28); Nobel Prize came in 1997 (age 56).
early_history_summary: Walker was born in Halifax, Yorkshire, the son of a stone mason and amateur pianist. He attended Rastrick Grammar School, specializing in physical sciences and mathematics, and went to St. Catherine's College, Oxford in 1960, receiving his BA in Chemistry in 1964. He began research on peptide antibiotics with E.P. Abraham at Oxford in 1965 and was awarded his D.Phil in 1969.
family_context_summary: Born in Halifax, Yorkshire; father was a stone mason and talented amateur pianist and vocalist. Brought up in a rural environment near Elland and then Rastrick with two younger sisters.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having scientific domain expertise; father was a stone mason with musical interests.
evidence_summary: Walker received a standard academic education at Oxford (BA 1964, D.Phil 1969) and did postdoctoral work in the US and France before joining the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology in Cambridge in 1974. His Nobel Prize-winning work on ATP synthase came in the 1990s. By age 26, he was a graduate student with no independently verifiable material milestone.

name: Jean Vuarnet
milestone_by_age_26: Won bronze in downhill at the 1958 FIS World Championships in Bad Gastein at age 25, after winning French national championships in all three disciplines (slalom, GS, downhill) in 1957.
early_history_summary: Born in Le Bardo, Tunisia, Vuarnet moved to Morzine, France as an infant and was introduced to skiing as a young child. He attended law school at the University of Grenoble, enrolling in 1952, and skied competitively. He trained under Georges Joubert, co-authored the influential book 'Ski ABC' in 1956, and won French national championships beginning in 1957.
primary_leverage_engine: Technical skiing innovation and alpine geography immersion
family_context_summary: Born in Le Bardo, Tunisia to a doctor father; family moved to Morzine, France when he was one year old. Parents divorced in 1943, after which he was sent to boarding schools in Paris and Lyon.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a doctor; no documented family background in skiing beyond the geographic accident of growing up in a ski resort town.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Morzine alpine geography, Georges Joubert coaching, French ski team, Ski ABC book, technique focus
evidence_summary: Vuarnet grew up in Morzine in the French Alps, providing direct immersion in ski culture from childhood. His sustained coaching relationship with Georges Joubert at the University of Grenoble was catalytic, producing both technical innovation (the aerodynamic tuck position) and co-authored books. Vuarnet believed himself not to be a natural skier and compensated through technique study. By age 25, he had won French national championships and a World Championship bronze medal. Family financial background is unclear due to parents' divorce and boarding school education.
starting_point: Born in Le Bardo, Tunisia to a doctor father; family moved to Morzine, France when he was one year old; parents divorced in 1943 and he was sent to boarding schools in Paris and Lyon.
current_position: Died in 2017 at age 83 in Sallanches, France; final role: Olympic gold medalist, developer of Avoriaz ski resort, and founder of Vuarnet eyewear brand.

trajectory.event: Won several races at the French University Games while studying law at the University of Grenoble.
Co-authored the influential technique book 'Ski ABC' with coach Georges Joubert.
Won French national championships in slalom, giant slalom, and downhill.
Won bronze in downhill at the FIS World Championships in Bad Gastein, Austria.
Won Olympic gold in downhill at Squaw Valley, becoming the first Olympic champion to use metal skis.
Launched development of the Avoriaz ski resort, which became part of the Portes du Soleil complex.
Died in Sallanches, France after a stroke.

name: Flavio Briatore
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1976), was working as a restaurant manager and insurance salesman in Italy after a failed restaurant. No material business milestone by age 26; his Benetton expansion and F1 career began in the 1980s.
early_history_summary: Briatore was born in Verzuolo near Cuneo in the Maritime Alps, the son of two school teachers. He failed public school twice and attended a private school, receiving a diploma in Land Surveying with the lowest grades. He worked as a ski instructor and restaurant manager, opening a restaurant named Tribüla that was unsuccessful. He then became a business assistant to Attilio Dutto, owner of a paint company, before moving to Milan to work in finance.
family_context_summary: Born in Verzuolo near Cuneo in the Maritime Alps, Italy; parents were both elementary school teachers. Modest background with no notable financial or business platform.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having business or motorsport domain expertise; parents were school teachers.
evidence_summary: Briatore's early career was marked by failed ventures and odd jobs. By age 26, he had opened and lost a restaurant, worked as a ski instructor and insurance salesman, and was an assistant to a paint company owner. His meeting with Luciano Benetton in 1974 and subsequent move to the US in 1982 to expand Benetton franchises was the turning point, but this came well after age 26. He was also convicted of fraudulent bankruptcy in the 1980s.

name: Jo Siffert
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1961 European Formula Junior Championship at age 25, then made his Formula One debut in 1962 at age 26, establishing himself as a professional racing driver at the highest level.
early_history_summary: Born in Fribourg, Switzerland to a poor dairy-owning family, Siffert had a deformed right foot requiring two operations. He left school at 16 and was apprenticed to a coachbuilding company. He began motorcycle racing in 1957, won the Swiss 350cc championship in 1959, then switched to car racing in 1960 with a Formula Junior Stanguellini. In 1961, he bought a Lotus 18 and won the European Formula Junior Championship despite being underfunded.
family_context_summary: Born in Fribourg, Switzerland to a poor family; father owned a small dairy. Siffert had a deformed right foot requiring two operations, leaving him with a pronounced limp. He found creative ways to earn money from a young age, including collecting scrap and trading cars.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as having motorsport connections; family ran a small dairy business.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, deformed foot, self-funded racing, coachbuilding apprenticeship, Swiss racing culture, team mechanics
evidence_summary: Siffert came from a poor family in Fribourg with a deformed right foot and no financial safety net. He financed his racing by collecting scrap, trading cars, and saving every cent from his coachbuilding apprenticeship. His mechanical knowledge from the apprenticeship provided direct domain exposure. Despite being underfunded, he won the 1961 European Formula Junior Championship and entered Formula One in 1962. His team mechanics (Oberson, Mader) and manager Blancpain formed a durable support team. No family domain advantage or financial platform is documented.
starting_point: Born in Fribourg, Switzerland to a poor family that owned a small dairy; had a deformed right foot requiring two operations, leaving a pronounced limp; left school at 16 for a coachbuilding apprenticeship.
current_position: Died in 1971 at age 35 in a racing crash at Brands Hatch, England; final role: BRM Formula One driver with two Grand Prix victories.

trajectory.event: Won the Swiss 350cc motorcycle championship, establishing himself in competitive racing.
Won the European Formula Junior Championship driving a Lotus 18, despite being underfunded.
Made Formula One debut as a privateer at the Monaco Grand Prix with a Lotus-Climax.
Won the British Grand Prix at Brands Hatch in Rob Walker's Lotus 49B, regarded as the last GP victory by a genuine privateer.
Won the Austrian Grand Prix with BRM; died in a crash at the World Championship Victory Race at Brands Hatch.

name: Grace Jones
milestone_by_age_26: By 1973 (age 25), had become one of the most prominent Black models of the 1970s, appearing on covers of Elle and Vogue Hommes and modeling for Yves St. Laurent and Kenzo in Paris after signing with Wilhelmina Models in New York.
early_history_summary: Born in Spanish Town, Jamaica, Jones was raised by her grandmother and an abusive step-grandfather in a strict Pentecostal household. She moved to the US at age 13 to join her parents in Syracuse, New York. She studied theater at Syracuse University before moving to New York City, where she signed with Wilhelmina Models. She then relocated to Paris, where her androgynous, bold appearance was embraced by the fashion industry.
primary_leverage_engine: Distinctive visual presence and fashion industry immersion
family_context_summary: Born in Spanish Town, Jamaica to Marjorie and Robert W. Jones, a local politician and Apostolic clergyman. Parents moved to the US, leaving children with their grandmother and an abusive step-grandfather ('Mas P'). Raised in strict Pentecostal faith with regular beatings. Joined parents in Syracuse, New York at age 13.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a local politician and Pentecostal minister who had been an agricultural laborer; no documented connections to fashion, music, or entertainment industries.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Paris fashion capital, Wilhelmina agency, distinctive appearance, abusive upbringing, Black model wave
evidence_summary: Jones overcame an abusive childhood in Jamaica under a strict Pentecostal regime before moving to the US at 13. Her distinctive androgynous appearance, initially rejected in New York, was embraced in Paris where she modeled for Yves St. Laurent, Kenzo, and was photographed by Helmut Newton and Guy Bourdin. The 1970s fashion industry's growing demand for Black models provided a structural wave. Her relocation to Paris and New York, the centers of global fashion, was catalytic. No family financial platform or domain advantage is documented; her success was driven by geographic relocation and distinctive physical presence.
starting_point: Born in Spanish Town, Jamaica to a local politician and Apostolic clergyman father and mother Marjorie; raised by an abusive step-grandfather in a strict Pentecostal household before joining parents in Syracuse, New York at age 13.
current_position: Active performer and cultural icon as of 2025; Order of Jamaica recipient; estimated net worth approximately $7 million; resides primarily in Europe.

trajectory.event: Began professional modeling career, signing with Wilhelmina Models in New York.
Established as one of the most prominent Black models in Paris, appearing on covers of Elle and Vogue Hommes and modeling for Yves St. Laurent.
Released debut album Portfolio on Island Records, launching her music career.
Released Nightclubbing, considered her breakthrough album with the hit 'Pull Up to the Bumper'.
Played May Day in the James Bond film A View to a Kill, gaining mainstream film recognition.
Released the documentary Grace Jones: Bloodlight and Bami, directed by Sophie Fiennes.

name: Alexey Pajitnov
milestone_by_age_26: Working as a computer programmer at the Dorodnitsyn Computing Centre on speech recognition; created Tetris in 1984 at age 28-29. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Pajitnov was born in Moscow to parents who were both writers; his father was an art critic and his mother a journalist. He studied applied mathematics at the Moscow Aviation Institute, graduating in 1979. He then accepted a job at the Dorodnitsyn Computing Centre of the Soviet Academy of Sciences, working on speech recognition. He created Tetris in 1984 while testing the capabilities of new computing equipment.
family_context_summary: Born in Moscow to Russian parents who were both writers; father was an art critic and mother was a journalist who wrote for newspapers and a film magazine. Parents divorced in 1967 when Pajitnov was 11; lived with his mother in a state-owned one-bedroom apartment before moving to a private apartment at age 17.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were both writers, providing exposure to the arts and cinema through his mother's film magazine work. No documented family background in computing or game design.
evidence_summary: Pajitnov graduated from the Moscow Aviation Institute in 1979 and worked on speech recognition at the Soviet Academy of Sciences. He created Tetris in 1984 (age 28-29) while testing new computing equipment, but did not receive royalties until 1996 when he co-founded The Tetris Company with Henk Rogers. By age 26, he was an early-career programmer with no independently verifiable material milestone. His parents' writing background provided arts exposure but no computing domain advantage.
